name: Fibromyalgia
summary: Graded exercise, education, sleep and pacing strategies are central. Manual therapy may offer temporary comfort but should not reinforce beliefs of tissue damage or fragility.

looksLike: Screen for alternative or coexisting medical conditions
redFlags: Inflammatory/systemic features inconsistent with known diagnosis
Unexplained major weight loss or fever
firstSteps: Assess widespread pain, fatigue, sleep, current activity and the patient's biggest functional limitation.
Start below the patient's flare threshold.
Choose an enjoyable form of aerobic activity plus simple strength.

assess: Screen for alternative or coexisting medical conditions

stages.label: Start: assess and set up
stages.goal: The goal is to build activity tolerance without reinforcing fear that normal movement is damaging tissue.

stages.label: Treat: build capacity
stages.goal: Use pacing, sleep support and graded exercise.
dose: Aerobic: start as low as 5–10 minutes and gradually build toward 20–30 minutes, 3–5 days/week.
Strength: 1–3 sets × 6–15 reps, 2–3 days/week, starting light.
Mobility: short daily sessions focused on comfort.
Aquatic exercise is an option if preferred.
moveOn: Increase one variable at a time
Use symptom-contingent flexibility rather than stopping all activity during mild flares

stages.goal: Manual therapy may provide comfort but should not become the only strategy.

dose: Increase one variable at a time—duration, then frequency, then intensity.

mistakes: Promising a tissue 'release' will cure widespread pain.
Changing the program every time symptoms fluctuate.

escalation: Coordinate multidisciplinary care when symptoms, sleep, mood or medication needs exceed physiotherapy scope
